examples.ko: 길에서 만 원을 주웠더니 공돈이 생긴 기분이에요.
examples.en: I found 10,000 won on the street and feel like I got free money.
I got a tax refund, so I'll spend it as if it's free money.
Free money slips away easily, so save it.

examples.ko: 친구가 갚은 돈을 공돈처럼 써 버렸어요.
examples.en: I spent the money my friend paid back as if it were a windfall.

examples.ko: 이 돈은 공돈이니까 맛있는 거 먹으러 가요.
examples.en: This is free money, so let's go eat something good.
Don't hope for easy money, work hard.

explain: 애쓰지 않았는데 뜻밖에 생긴 돈에 써요. '생기다, 들어오다'와 자주 쓰고, 기분 좋게 쓰는 돈이라는 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.example: 오랜만에 입은 옷 주머니에서 만 원이 나와서 공돈이 생겼어요.
phrases.en: I found 10,000 won in the pocket of a coat I hadn't worn in a while, so I got some free money.
phrases.nuance_ko: '생기다'와 함께 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the most common pairing, with '생기다'.

phrases.example: 공돈을 쓰는 날은 친구들에게 커피를 사요.
phrases.en: On days I spend windfall money, I buy my friends coffee.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻밖에 생긴 돈을 가볍게 쓴다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It carries a feeling of spending unexpected money lightly.

phrases.example: 이건 공돈이에요, 같이 맛있는 거 먹어요.
phrases.en: This is free money, so let's eat something nice together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 받은 돈이 노력 없이 생긴 돈임을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to say that money came without any effort.

explain_en: It is used for money that came unexpectedly without any effort. It often goes with '생기다' or '들어오다' and has a cheerful feeling of money to enjoy spending.

examples.ko: 입학식 날 모두 함께 교가를 불렀어요.
examples.en: On the day of the entrance ceremony, we all sang the school song together.

examples.ko: 우리 학교 교가는 가사가 참 멋져요.
examples.en: Our school song has really nice lyrics.
Even though I've graduated, I still remember the school song.

examples.ko: 교가에 우리 학교 산 이름이 나와요.
examples.en: The name of the mountain by our school appears in the school song.
There's a part of the sports day where we sing the school song.
Memorizing the lyrics of the school song is our homework.

explain: 학교마다 하나씩 있는 노래라서 입학식, 졸업식, 체육대회 같은 행사에서 불러요. '교가를 부르다'로 자주 써요. 학교의 가르침을 담은 말은 '교훈'이라고 해요.

phrases.example: 졸업한 지 오래됐지만 교가를 아직도 외우고 있어요.
phrases.en: It's been a long time since I graduated, but I still remember the school song.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가사를 보지 않고 기억한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means remembering the words without looking.
phrases.en_equiv: to know the school song by heart

phrases.en: The school song rang out across the playground.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사에서 노래가 크게 들릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the song is heard loudly at an event.

phrases.example: 입학식에서 학교 노래를 다 같이 불렀어요.
phrases.en: We all sang the school song together at the entrance ceremony.
phrases.nuance_ko: '교가'를 쉽게 풀어 말한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy way to say '교가' in plain words.

explain_en: Every school has one, and it is sung at events like entrance ceremonies, graduations and sports days. It is commonly used as '교가를 부르다'. The saying that expresses a school's teaching is called '교훈'.

en: to act frivolously; to act carelessly

examples.en: My younger sibling was careless and broke a cup.
Don't be careless; check slowly.
That's why you keep losing things when you're so careless.
The child came running down the stairs in a hurry.
My older brother is hasty by nature, so he makes many mistakes.
I want to fix my habit of being careless.

explain: 침착하지 못하고 서두르다가 실수하는 모습이에요. '덤벙대다'와 뜻이 같고, 비슷한 말로 '덜렁대다'가 있어요. 반대로 차분한 사람은 '침착하다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling is always careless and loses things.
phrases.nuance_ko: '덤벙거리다'와 거의 같은 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same meaning as '덤벙거리다'.

phrases.en: I was careless and left my wallet behind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 말로, 조심성 없이 행동하는 모습에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word for acting without care.

phrases.en: I'm the careless type, so I often make mistakes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 성격을 말할 때 쓰는 꼴이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A form used to describe a person's personality.

explain_en: It describes rushing without calm and making mistakes. It means the same as '덤벙대다', and a similar word is '덜렁대다'. A calm person is described as '침착하다'.

examples.ko: 경기 막판에 우리 팀이 골을 넣었어요.
examples.en: Our team scored in the last moments of the game.

examples.ko: 막판까지 누가 이길지 알 수 없었어요.
examples.en: We could not tell who would win until the very end.

examples.ko: 저는 시험 막판에 답을 고쳐서 틀렸어요.
examples.en: I changed an answer at the last minute of the test and got it wrong.

examples.ko: 막판 뒤집기로 드라마 같은 결과가 나왔어요.
examples.en: A last-minute comeback gave a dramatic result.
The work reached its final stage and got busier.
The plan changed at the last moment and everyone panicked.

explain: 막판은 일이나 경기가 끝나 가는 마지막 부분이에요. '마지막'보다 긴장되고 급한 느낌이 있어서 '막판 스퍼트', '막판 뒤집기'처럼 써요. 말할 때 자주 나오는 편한 표현이에요.

phrases.en: The score flipped at the very end.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '에'를 붙여 끝나기 직전의 때를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds the particle 에 to mean right near the end.

phrases.en: Our team succeeded in a last-minute comeback.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끝나기 직전에 결과를 바꾸는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means turning the result around right before the end.

phrases.en: Don't give up until the very last moment.
phrases.nuance_ko: '막판'과 비슷하지만 조금 더 부드러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 막판 but a bit softer in tone.

explain_en: 막판 is the very last part of a task or game, just before it ends. It feels tenser and more urgent than 마지막, as in 막판 스퍼트 (final sprint) and 막판 뒤집기 (last-minute comeback). It is a casual word that comes up often in speech.

en: collecting payment at a counter; storage

examples.en: This room doesn't have enough storage space.
I saw the doctor and then paid at the hospital desk.
I bought storage furniture and tidied up my room.

examples.ko: 침대 아래에 수납 서랍이 있어서 편해요.
examples.en: There are storage drawers under the bed, which is convenient.
Please pay at the window on the first floor.
I like bags that hold things well.

explain: 집에서는 물건을 넣어 두는 '수납'이고, 병원·학원에서는 돈을 내는 곳인 '수납 창구'를 가리켜요. 같은 단어가 두 가지로 쓰이니 장소를 보고 구별하세요. 집에서는 '수납장', '수납공간'처럼 뒤에 말이 붙는 때가 많아요.

phrases.en: The new house has plenty of storage space, which I like.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집에서 물건을 넣어 두는 공간을 말할 때 가장 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common term for space at home where you keep things.

phrases.en: I bought a small storage cabinet for the living room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 넣어 두는 가구 자체를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the piece of furniture used for storing things.

phrases.example: 진료가 끝나면 수납 창구에서 돈을 내세요.
phrases.en: After your appointment, please pay at the payment counter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원이나 학원에서 돈을 내는 곳을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The place in a hospital or academy where you pay.

explain_en: At home 수납 is about putting things away, while at hospitals and academies it points to the '수납 창구' where you pay. The same word has two uses, so tell them apart by the place. At home it often comes with another word, as in '수납장' or '수납공간'.

examples.en: Oops, I left my wallet at home.

examples.ko: 아차 하는 순간에 컵이 바닥에 떨어졌어요.
examples.en: In the moment I said 'oops,' the cup fell to the floor.

examples.ko: 시험 중에 아차 싶어서 답을 고쳤어요.
examples.en: During the test I realized my mistake and fixed the answer.
Oops, today was my friend's birthday!

examples.ko: 버스에서 내린 뒤에야 아차 하고 우산을 떠올렸어요.
examples.en: Only after getting off the bus did I suddenly remember my umbrella.

examples.ko: 아차 싶었지만 열쇠는 이미 문 안에 있었어요.
examples.en: I realized my mistake, but the key was already inside the door.

explain: '아차 하다', '아차 싶다'처럼 문장 안에서도 쓰고, 혼잣말로 '아차!'만 말하기도 해요. '아이고'는 힘들거나 놀랄 때 하는 말이고, 아차는 '내가 놓쳤구나' 하고 갑자기 깨달을 때 나와요. 비슷한 말로 '앗'도 있어요.

phrases.en: The moment I stepped out the door, I realized I'd messed up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실수를 깨달은 마음을 문장 안에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used inside a sentence to describe realizing a mistake.

phrases.en: Oops! I didn't bring my umbrella.
phrases.nuance_ko: 혼자 말하듯 짧게 외칠 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as a short exclamation, like talking to yourself.

phrases.en: Oh no, I left my phone behind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 말이에요. 앗은 놀라거나 순간 깨달을 때 가볍게 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word; 앗 comes out lightly with surprise or sudden realization.

explain_en: You can use it inside a sentence as 아차 하다 or 아차 싶다, or just mutter '아차!' to yourself. 아이고 is for being tired or surprised, while 아차 comes when you suddenly realize you missed something. 앗 is a similar word.

examples.en: I am transferring to another school next month.
My friend transferred to a school in Busan.

examples.ko: 전학하면 새 친구를 사귀어야 해서 걱정돼요.
examples.en: If I transfer, I have to make new friends, so I am worried.
I was very nervous on my first day after transferring.

examples.ko: 내년에 전학할 거라서 이사 준비를 해요.
examples.en: I am going to transfer next year, so I am preparing to move.
I wrote a letter to the friend who is transferring.

explain: 초·중·고등학교에서 다른 학교로 옮길 때 써요. 대학교에서 옮기는 것은 보통 '편입하다'라고 해요. 같은 학교 안에서 반을 바꾸는 것과도 달라요. '~(으)로 전학하다', '전학을 가다/오다'로 써요.

phrases.en: I'm transferring to a school in Seoul next year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 내가 다른 학교로 옮겨 갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you move to another school.

phrases.example: 새 친구가 우리 반에 전학을 왔어요.
phrases.en: A new friend transferred into our class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 학교에서 우리 학교로 올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone comes from another school to ours.

phrases.en: The transfer student introduced himself.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전학해서 온 학생을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A student who has transferred in.

explain_en: Used for moving to another school at the elementary, middle, or high school level. For universities, people usually say '편입하다'. It is also different from changing classes within one school. Use '~(으)로 전학하다' or '전학을 가다/오다'.

examples.en: Popular items sell out quickly.
I tried to order it, but it was already sold out.
These shoes will be sold out by tomorrow.
Will the sold-out book come back in stock?
Most things sold out on the first day of the sale, which was a pity.
We ran out of stock and it ended up sold out.

explain: 쇼핑몰에서 상품 옆에 '품절'이라고 쓰여 있으면 지금 살 수 없다는 표시예요. 가게 주인이 말할 때는 '다 팔렸어요', '재고가 없어요'라고도 해요. 다시 들어오면 '재입고'라고 부르니 같이 알아 두면 좋아요.

phrases.en: Those shoes are sold out right now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쇼핑몰에서 상품 옆에 쓰는 가장 흔한 명사 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common noun usage, shown next to products on shopping sites.

phrases.en: The bread was all sold in the morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게에서 말할 때는 '품절되다' 대신 쉽게 쓸 수 있는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy alternative to 품절되다 when speaking in a shop.

phrases.en: Order quickly before it sells out.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-기 전에'를 붙여 상품이 없어지기 전에 하라고 권할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -기 전에 urges someone to act before the item runs out.

explain_en: On a shopping site, 품절 next to an item means you cannot buy it right now. A shop owner speaking aloud may also say 다 팔렸어요 or 재고가 없어요. When it comes back in stock it is called 재입고, which is worth learning together.

examples.ko: 필요 없는 물건을 사서 헛돈만 썼어요.
examples.en: I bought things I didn't need and just wasted money.

examples.ko: 이 학원은 효과가 없어서 헛돈 쓴 기분이에요.
examples.en: This academy doesn't work, so I feel like I wasted my money.
I keep a household account book so I don't waste money.

examples.ko: 고쳐도 또 고장 나면 헛돈이 될까 봐 걱정이에요.
examples.en: I'm worried it will be wasted money if it breaks again after the repair.
I bought it because it was on sale and ended up throwing money away.

examples.ko: 헛돈 들이지 말고 꼭 필요한 것만 사세요.
examples.en: Don't waste money; buy only what you really need.

explain: '헛-'은 보람 없이 한다는 느낌을 더해요. '헛돈을 쓰다', '헛돈을 들이다', '헛돈을 날리다'처럼 자주 말해요. 비슷한 '돈 낭비'보다 아깝다는 감정이 더 강해요.

phrases.en: I lost my money for nothing on stocks.
phrases.nuance_ko: '쓰다'보다 돈이 아무 소용없이 사라졌다는 느낌이 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Stronger than 'spend': the money disappeared with nothing to show for it.

phrases.example: 고장 난 차에 헛돈을 들이고 싶지 않아요.
phrases.en: I don't want to put money into a broken car for nothing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일에 돈을 들였는데 결과가 없을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you invest money in something and get no result.

phrases.en: This method just costs money for nothing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈이 나가는 것을 주어로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the money spent is the subject of the sentence.

explain_en: The prefix '헛-' adds a sense of doing something in vain. It is often used as '헛돈을 쓰다', '헛돈을 들이다', or '헛돈을 날리다'. Compared with '돈 낭비', it carries a stronger feeling of regret.
